reason: Reply A makes "what happens next time" a section of the email itself, and that answers this reader's real complaint: the farm went quiet and gave no credit. It would lead the user to put the weekly emails and the weather credit into the piece. A also drops the $31,000 and the scarcity pressure, both of which could put off someone who felt shortchanged. Reply B asks about a crop-loss policy only as an open question and leaves it out of its order for the email, so the piece built from B is more likely to miss the commitment that wins this reader back.
